# Applied Science Manager Phone Screen — Project Deep-Dive + Leadership BQ

[← Amazon](../README.md) · [Every Amazon question](../../amazon.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/asm-phone-screen-deep-dive-bq)

`deep-dive`

---

## Requirements

- Structure: 60 minutes total — roughly 30 minutes for a resume and project deep-dive, followed by 30 minutes of leadership behavioral questions. There is no self-introduction; the interviewer reviews the resume beforehand and selects two projects to discuss.
- Technical-project probes (using a search-ranking example): what motivated the project and what business problem it solved; which choices were personally yours; why this particular model was chosen over alternatives; how success was defined, including both offline and online metrics; the design of the A/B test; how you would debug a situation where online results fall short of expectations; the most difficult technical obstacle and how it was overcome; what you would do differently if you could redo the project.
- Management-project probes: the size and structure of the team; how you established the technical direction and roadmap; cross-functional coordination with product management, engineering, and business stakeholders; how projects were prioritized; how you measure the success of your team.
- Behavioral stems: resolving a conflict within your own team; coaching a team member who was underperforming; motivating a team through a tough project or period of low morale; a difficult leadership decision you had to make.

## Notes

- Using the STAR method is not the end of a question — expect recursive follow-ups: why you chose that approach, what alternatives you considered, what you would change, the quantified outcomes, how the team member developed over time, and the lessons you took away. Stories where you were not the primary decision-maker fall apart quickly under this pattern.
- Every project on your resume should be able to support 10–15 minutes of continuous questioning around the "why," "how," and "what-if."
- The pacing is brisk but the tone remains friendly; with behavioral questions taking half the hour, any thinness in management experience is heavily exposed.

## Preparation

- For each project on your resume, script a 10–15 minute walkthrough that covers the motivation, your specific decisions, offline and online metrics, the experiment design, and one debugging story.
- Build a bank of manager stories — a team conflict, a low performer, a morale dip, a hard call — each one containing a quantified result and an explicit beat for lessons learned.
